## Courtesy citations (public domain)

- Occupational codes follow O*NET-SOC 2019, which is based on the 2018 Standard Occupational Classification, U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (https://www.bls.gov/soc/). BLS asks that it be cited as the source (https://www.bls.gov/opub/copyright-information.htm).

## Rules that travel with the data

- Keep the version number in the O*NET® credit ("O*NET 31.0 Database", not "O*NET Database").
- Keep the modification and non-endorsement sentences whenever O*NET® values have been edited, filtered, ranked or combined.
- Use "O*NET" only as an adjective followed by a generic noun ("built with O*NET® data"), with the ® symbol, never possessive or plural, and never in a way that implies USDOL/ETA sponsorship or endorsement.
- Do not add terms or technical measures that restrict a recipient's CC BY 4.0 rights in the O*NET®-derived values.

Package 0.0.1 is a skeleton and ships no O*NET® values; the text above applies to every later version that does.
